Usage: canvasnet info <input> [--page N | --all-pages] [--json]

Reads only the file header: the format, the pixel size, the channels, whether it has transparency,
the number of frames of a GIF, and the EXIF orientation of a JPEG. An SVG reports its intrinsic size.
A PDF, PPTX, or VSDX document reports its number of pages and the size of a page (the first, or the
one chosen with --page, or every page with --all-pages): in pixels at 96 dpi and in points, the
rotation of a PDF page, and the name of a VSDX page. An OpenSCAD model is parsed (not evaluated) and
reports the modules and functions it defines and its include and use directives. A Vega-Lite chart
(.vl.json or .vl) is parsed and measured (not drawn) and reports the size it is laid out at, and the
marks, data references, parameters, title, and schema version of its specification. A Mermaid diagram
(.mmd or .mermaid) is parsed and measured (not drawn) and reports the size it is laid out at, its type
(and whether this version draws it), direction, titles, and numbers of nodes, edges, and subgraphs
('canvasnet help mermaid' says what each diagram type counts). The input may end in a
fragment (report.pdf#page=2) as for 'render'; only the page is used here: the other parameters are checked
(a value that cannot be used is an error) and otherwise ignored, and an unknown or repeated parameter is a
warning on standard error.

Examples:
  canvasnet info photo.jpg
  canvasnet info report.pdf --all-pages
  canvasnet info part.scad --json
  canvasnet info chart.vl.json --json
  canvasnet info flow.mmd --json
  canvasnet info drawing.svg --json

Show the format, size, and properties of an image or drawing without rendering it

Options:
  --page <N>   For a document, describe this page or slide, counted from 1 (default 1)
  --all-pages  For a document, describe every page or slide

Global options:
  -v, --version               Display version information

Usage: canvasnet crop <input> <geometry> -o <output> [options]

Cuts out the rectangle x,y,w,h or WxH+X+Y (origin and size), each value in pixels (10 or 10px) or percent (10%).

'crop' is 'render' with this one operation first, so it takes every option of render (--page, --dpi,
--background, --format, --quality, --no-clobber, --json, ...). The operations given as options
(--crop, --resize, --fit, --rotate, --flip, --pad, --grayscale, --threshold, --deskew, --trim, --grid, ...)
are applied after it, in the order written. The input may end in a fragment such as report.pdf#page=3 or
part.scad#view=top (quote it in a shell), as for 'render'.

Examples:
  canvasnet crop photo.png 10,10,200,100 -o part.png
  canvasnet crop photo.png 200x100+10+10 -o part.png

# Size and resource limits

Size and resource limits and the errors they produce.

The largest sizes and budgets the tool accepts, and the error each one produces.

## Images and output

- **Image side**: At most 8192 pixels on a side for any image the
  tool reads, draws, or writes; a larger size is refused with size-limit before
  any pixels are allocated. 'canvasnet formats' reports it as maxDimension.
- `--dpi`: Above 0 and at most 2400 (PDF, PPTX, VSDX; a VSDX needs a whole
  number). The default is 96. A page is its size in points times the dpi divided
  by 72.
- `--quality`: JPEG quality 1 to 100, default
  90.
- **Memory**: An image 8192 by 8192 pixels uses about
  256 MB per copy, so large pipelines need memory.

## OpenSCAD models

- `--max-triangles`: Default 5000000 triangles; a model that needs
  more fails with budget-exceeded. A model source longer than the library reads
  is corrupt-input.
- **Default size**: 800x800 pixels unless --size, --width, --height, or --scale
  is given.

## Vega-Lite charts

- **Specification**: At most 4194304 characters (corrupt-input)
  and JSON nesting depth 64 (vega-lite-error).
- **Data files**: At most 64 files, 67108864 bytes per
  file, and 1000000 rows in total; beyond that the chart fails with
  budget-exceeded.
- **Pictures**: At most 256 different pictures (image marks); beyond
  that the chart fails with budget-exceeded.
- **Painting**: At most 250000000 device pixels painted in one
  render (fills, strokes, text, and pictures that cover the image count by the
  area they cover, so marks with huge sizes or stroke widths, or pictures
  without a size, are stopped); beyond that the chart fails with
  budget-exceeded, located at the mark.
- **Size**: A chart that lays out larger than 8192 pixels on a side
  is size-limit.
